decks.title: Benzaldehyde — Part 1: Preparation, properties and addition reactions
goals: Write the Etard reaction and other preparations of benzaldehyde
Describe the physical properties of benzaldehyde
Write oxidation, reduction and nucleophilic addition reactions of benzaldehyde
Write the products with hydroxylamine, hydrazine, phenylhydrazine and PCl₅

slides.heading: Benzaldehyde
slides.body_md: Part 1 — C₆H₅CHO: the simplest aromatic aldehyde, its preparation and its addition reactions.

visual.alt: Table of uses and occurrence of benzaldehyde

slides.narration: Namaste! The smell of bitter almonds comes from benzaldehyde, the simplest aromatic aldehyde, with an aldehyde group attached directly to a benzene ring. It flavours foods, scents soaps and is a starting material for dyes and drugs. In this part we see how it is prepared, what it looks like, and how its aldehyde group reacts.

slides.heading: Structure
slides.body_md: In C₆H₅CHO the –CHO carbon is **sp²** and **conjugated** with the ring. Benzaldehyde has **no α-hydrogen** (the carbon next to C=O is a ring carbon with no H to lose as an enolate), so it cannot undergo aldol self-condensation. Conjugation slightly reduces the δ+ on the carbonyl carbon, so it is a little less reactive than aliphatic aldehydes.

visual.alt: Table comparing benzaldehyde and ethanal

slides.narration: The aldehyde group in benzaldehyde sits directly on the ring, and its double bond is conjugated with the ring’s pi electrons, which slightly reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon. Importantly, the carbon next to the carbonyl group is part of the ring and carries no hydrogen that can be removed, so benzaldehyde has no alpha hydrogen. This decides much of its chemistry.

slides.heading: Laboratory preparation: the Etard reaction
slides.body_md: Toluene is oxidised by **chromyl chloride** (CrO₂Cl₂) in CS₂ or CCl₄; a brown chromium complex (Etard complex) separates, which is hydrolysed by water to benzaldehyde. Mild oxidation stops at the aldehyde. Other routes: side-chain chlorination of toluene to benzal chloride and hydrolysis; Gattermann–Koch (benzene + CO + HCl, AlCl₃/CuCl).

visual.alt: Flow of the Etard reaction

slides.narration: In the laboratory, benzaldehyde is made by the Etard reaction. Chromyl chloride in carbon disulphide gently oxidises the methyl group of toluene, forming a brown complex. Water breaks down the complex to give benzaldehyde, without further oxidation to benzoic acid. Benzaldehyde can also be made by chlorinating the side chain of toluene to benzal chloride and hydrolysing it, or from benzene, carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride.

slides.heading: Worked example: routes from toluene
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Give two ways of converting toluene into benzaldehyde, and explain why acidified KMnO₄ is not used.

**Route 1 (Etard).** CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂, then hydrolysis with water.

**Route 2.** Cl₂ in sunlight (boiling toluene) gives benzal chloride; heating with water at 373 K gives benzaldehyde.

**KMnO₄** is too strong: it oxidises the side chain all the way to **benzoic acid**.

visual.alt: Table of products from toluene

slides.narration: Both routes stop at the aldehyde. In the Etard reaction, the chromium complex protects the aldehyde from further oxidation until water is added. In the second route, two chlorines are put on the methyl carbon and then replaced by an oxygen on hydrolysis. Potassium permanganate is too strong an oxidant: it converts the methyl group all the way to a carboxylic acid group.

slides.heading: Physical properties
slides.body_md: Colourless oily liquid with a smell of **bitter almonds**; b.p. 452 K; slightly soluble in water, miscible with organic solvents; denser than water (1.04 g cm⁻³). On standing in air it slowly **oxidises to benzoic acid** (white crystals appear around the stopper).

visual.alt: Table of physical properties of benzaldehyde

slides.narration: Benzaldehyde is a colourless oily liquid that smells of bitter almonds. It boils at four hundred and fifty two kelvin, is only slightly soluble in water and mixes with organic solvents. Old bottles often show white crystals around the neck: air has slowly oxidised some of the benzaldehyde to benzoic acid.

slides.heading: Quick check: preparation and properties
slides.body_md: Identify the Etard reagent or a property of benzaldehyde.
slides.narration: Quick check. Chromyl chloride stops at the aldehyde; air slowly turns benzaldehyde into benzoic acid.

slides.heading: Oxidation and reduction
slides.body_md: **Oxidation:** air, acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or alkaline KMnO₄ → benzoic acid; **Tollens’ reagent → silver mirror**; but **Fehling’s solution is not reduced** (aromatic aldehyde). **Reduction:** H₂/Ni, NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄ → **benzyl alcohol** (phenylmethanol); Zn–Hg/HCl (Clemmensen) or Wolff–Kishner → **toluene**.

visual.alt: Table of oxidation and reduction of benzaldehyde

slides.narration: Benzaldehyde is easily oxidised to benzoic acid, even by air, and it gives a silver mirror with Tollens’ reagent. Unlike aliphatic aldehydes, however, it does not reduce Fehling’s solution. Reduction with hydrogen and nickel or with sodium borohydride gives benzyl alcohol, while the Clemmensen or Wolff–Kishner method removes the oxygen completely to give toluene.

slides.heading: Nucleophilic addition: HCN and NaHSO₃
slides.body_md: Benzaldehyde adds nucleophiles at the carbonyl carbon. **HCN** gives **mandelonitrile** (benzaldehyde cyanohydrin), hydrolysed to **mandelic acid**. **NaHSO₃** gives a crystalline bisulphite adduct (used to separate benzaldehyde).

slides.narration: Like other aldehydes, benzaldehyde adds nucleophiles. Cyanide ions attack the carbonyl carbon, and protonation gives mandelonitrile, which acid hydrolysis converts into mandelic acid, two-hydroxy-two-phenylethanoic acid. Sodium hydrogensulphite forms a crystalline adduct, which can be filtered off and decomposed again: a convenient way to separate benzaldehyde from other substances.

slides.heading: Ammonia derivatives and PCl₅
slides.body_md: Ammonia derivatives add and eliminate water (C=O → C=N). **PCl₅** replaces the carbonyl oxygen by two chlorines, giving **benzal chloride**.

visual.alt: Table of reactions with ammonia derivatives and PCl₅

slides.narration: Hydroxylamine, hydrazine and phenylhydrazine react with benzaldehyde by addition followed by loss of water, giving benzaldoxime, the hydrazone and the phenylhydrazone, all crystalline solids useful for identification. Phosphorus pentachloride swaps the carbonyl oxygen for two chlorine atoms, giving benzal chloride, the same compound obtained by chlorinating the side chain of toluene.

slides.heading: Worked example: products of benzaldehyde
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Give the product of benzaldehyde with (a) LiAlH₄; (b) HCN, then H₃O⁺ and heat; (c) phenylhydrazine; (d) PCl₅; (e) Zn–Hg/HCl.

**(a)** Benzyl alcohol, $\ce{C6H5CH2OH}$.

**(b)** Mandelic acid, $\ce{C6H5CH(OH)COOH}$ (via mandelonitrile).

**(c)** Benzaldehyde phenylhydrazone, $\ce{C6H5CH=NNHC6H5}$.

**(d)** Benzal chloride, $\ce{C6H5CHCl2}$.

**(e)** Toluene, $\ce{C6H5CH3}$.

visual.alt: Table of products

slides.narration: Work through each reagent. Lithium aluminium hydride reduces the aldehyde to benzyl alcohol. Hydrogen cyanide gives the cyanohydrin, and hydrolysing its nitrile group gives mandelic acid. Phenylhydrazine gives the phenylhydrazone. Phosphorus pentachloride gives benzal chloride. And the Clemmensen reagents reduce the CHO group right down to a methyl group.

slides.heading: Quick check: addition reactions
slides.body_md: Predict the product of benzaldehyde with an addition or ammonia-derivative reagent.
slides.narration: Quick check. Addition across the carbonyl group, or addition followed by loss of water.

slides.heading: Quick check: oxidation and reduction
slides.body_md: Decide whether benzaldehyde reduces a given reagent, or what it is reduced to.
slides.narration: Quick check. Tollens’ yes, Fehling’s no; hydride gives benzyl alcohol, Clemmensen gives toluene.

slides.heading: Summary: Part 1
bullets: No α-H; CHO conjugated with ring.
Etard: toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ (CS₂), then H₂O; also benzal chloride hydrolysis and Gattermann–Koch.
Colourless oil, bitter almond smell, b.p. 452 K; air-oxidised to benzoic acid.
Tollens’ positive, Fehling’s negative; reduction → benzyl alcohol or toluene.
HCN → mandelonitrile; NaHSO₃ adduct; oxime, hydrazone, phenylhydrazone; PCl₅ → benzal chloride.

visual.alt: Summary table

slides.narration: Let us sum up Part 1. Benzaldehyde has no alpha hydrogen and its aldehyde group is conjugated with the ring. It is made in the laboratory by the Etard reaction. It is easily oxidised to benzoic acid and reduces Tollens’ reagent but not Fehling’s solution. It adds hydrogen cyanide and sodium hydrogensulphite, forms derivatives with ammonia derivatives, and gives benzal chloride with phosphorus pentachloride.

slides.heading: Exam tips: Part 1
bullets: Name chromyl chloride and the solvent (CS₂) for the Etard reaction.
Benzaldehyde reduces Tollens’ but not Fehling’s.
PCl₅ gives benzal chloride, not benzoyl chloride.

rows: Benzaldehyde gives red ppt with Fehling’s

visual.alt: Table of three common slips in Part 1 and fixes

slides.narration: Some tips. For the Etard reaction, name chromyl chloride and carbon disulphide. Remember that benzaldehyde gives the Tollens’ test but not the Fehling’s test. The cyanohydrin is mandelonitrile. And phosphorus pentachloride gives benzal chloride, not benzoyl chloride, which comes from benzoic acid.

decks.title: Benzaldehyde — Part 2: Named reactions, ring substitution and tests
goals: Write equations for the Cannizzaro, benzoin and Perkin reactions of benzaldehyde
Explain why the –CHO group is meta directing and write ring substitution reactions
Distinguish benzaldehyde from aliphatic aldehydes and state its uses

slides.heading: Benzaldehyde’s special reactions
slides.body_md: Part 2 — reactions that depend on having no α-hydrogen, and substitution on the ring.

visual.alt: Flow of the reactions in Part 2

slides.narration: Because benzaldehyde has no alpha hydrogen, it shows reactions that aliphatic aldehydes like ethanal do not: the Cannizzaro reaction, the benzoin condensation and, with acetic anhydride, the Perkin reaction. Its ring also undergoes substitution, but the aldehyde group sends new groups to the meta position. We end with tests and uses.

slides.heading: Cannizzaro reaction
slides.body_md: With **concentrated** NaOH or KOH, benzaldehyde **disproportionates**: one molecule is reduced to **benzyl alcohol**, the other oxidised to **sodium benzoate** (acidify → benzoic acid). OH⁻ adds to one C=O; the intermediate transfers a **hydride ion** to a second molecule.

visual.alt: Flow of the Cannizzaro mechanism

slides.narration: With concentrated sodium hydroxide, half the benzaldehyde is oxidised and half reduced. Hydroxide adds to one molecule, and the tetrahedral anion pushes a hydride ion onto the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule. The first becomes benzoic acid, as its sodium salt, and the second becomes benzyl alcohol. The products are separated by extraction, and acidification releases benzoic acid.

slides.heading: Benzoin condensation
slides.body_md: Benzaldehyde heated with **ethanolic KCN** (CN⁻ catalyst) dimerises to **benzoin**, an α-hydroxy ketone: 2-hydroxy-1,2-diphenylethan-1-one.

visual.alt: Table of the benzoin condensation

slides.narration: When benzaldehyde is warmed with potassium cyanide in ethanol, two molecules join to give benzoin, which has a hydroxyl group on one carbon and a ketone group on the next. Cyanide acts only as a catalyst: it adds to one molecule, makes its former carbonyl carbon able to attack a second molecule, and is released again at the end.

slides.heading: Perkin reaction
slides.body_md: Benzaldehyde is heated (about 453 K) with **acetic anhydride** and **sodium acetate**; the product is **cinnamic acid** (3-phenylprop-2-enoic acid), an α,β-unsaturated acid.

visual.alt: Table of the Perkin reaction

slides.narration: In the Perkin reaction, benzaldehyde is heated with acetic anhydride and sodium acetate. The acetate ion removes a hydrogen from the anhydride, and the resulting anion attacks the benzaldehyde carbonyl. After loss of water and hydrolysis, cinnamic acid is formed, with a carbon–carbon double bond between the ring and the acid group. Cinnamic acid and its esters are used in perfumes and flavours.

slides.heading: Worked example: three named reactions
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Identify the reaction and product: (a) benzaldehyde + 50% KOH; (b) benzaldehyde + KCN in ethanol, warm; (c) benzaldehyde + (CH₃CO)₂O + CH₃COONa, 453 K; (d) benzaldehyde + methanal + conc. NaOH.

**(a)** Cannizzaro: benzyl alcohol + potassium benzoate.

**(b)** Benzoin condensation: benzoin.

**(c)** Perkin: cinnamic acid.

**(d)** Crossed Cannizzaro: benzyl alcohol + sodium methanoate.

visual.alt: Table of named reactions of benzaldehyde

slides.narration: Recognise each reaction by its reagent. Concentrated alkali alone: Cannizzaro. Cyanide in ethanol: benzoin condensation. Acetic anhydride with sodium acetate on heating: Perkin. With methanal and concentrated alkali, methanal is the one oxidised, so all the benzaldehyde becomes benzyl alcohol, which is a useful way to make it.

slides.heading: Quick check: named reactions
slides.body_md: Match a reagent to the named reaction and product.
slides.narration: Quick check. Concentrated alkali, ethanolic cyanide, or anhydride with acetate.

slides.heading: Electrophilic substitution: meta direction
slides.body_md: The –CHO group withdraws electrons (−I and −R), **deactivating** the ring; positive charge in the σ-complex is placed on the carbon bearing CHO for o/p attack (destabilised), but not for meta attack. So substitution is **meta** and slower than in benzene.

visual.alt: Table of electrophilic substitution of benzaldehyde

slides.narration: The aldehyde group pulls electrons out of the ring, both through the sigma bond and by resonance, so the ring reacts more slowly than benzene. Resonance structures show that attack at ortho or para positions would place positive charge right next to the electron-withdrawing group, which is unfavourable, while meta attack avoids this. So nitration, chlorination and sulphonation all give meta products.

slides.heading: Worked example: meta products
slides.body_md:
**Problem.** Give the major product of benzaldehyde with (a) conc. HNO₃/H₂SO₄ in the cold, (b) Br₂/FeBr₃. Why is the nitration done in the cold?

**(a)** 3-Nitrobenzaldehyde. **(b)** 3-Bromobenzaldehyde.

**Cold:** the –CHO group is easily oxidised by hot nitric acid (to –COOH), so a low temperature keeps the aldehyde intact.

visual.alt: Table of meta products

slides.narration: Both electrophilic substitutions go meta to the aldehyde group, giving three-nitrobenzaldehyde and three-bromobenzaldehyde. Nitration is carried out at low temperature because hot concentrated nitric acid would also oxidise the aldehyde group to a carboxylic acid group.

slides.heading: Quick check: ring substitution
slides.body_md: Predict the position of electrophilic substitution in benzaldehyde.
slides.narration: Quick check. The aldehyde group is electron-withdrawing and meta directing.

slides.heading: Aromatic versus aliphatic aldehydes
slides.body_md: Tests that distinguish **benzaldehyde** from **ethanal** (or other aliphatic aldehydes):

visual.alt: Table of tests distinguishing benzaldehyde from ethanal

slides.narration: Several tests tell benzaldehyde from aliphatic aldehydes such as ethanal. Fehling’s solution is reduced by ethanal but not by benzaldehyde. Ethanal gives iodoform; benzaldehyde does not. Ethanal undergoes aldol reactions with alkali, while benzaldehyde, with no alpha hydrogen, gives the Cannizzaro reaction. Tollens’ reagent, however, is reduced by both.

slides.heading: Uses of benzaldehyde
slides.body_md: Flavouring (almond, cherry); perfumes and soaps; manufacture of **dyes** (malachite green), **cinnamic acid** (Perkin), **mandelic acid** (via HCN) and **benzoin**; as a solvent for some resins.

visual.alt: Table of products made from benzaldehyde

slides.narration: Benzaldehyde is used directly as an almond flavouring and in perfumes and soaps. It is also a starting material: the Perkin reaction gives cinnamic acid, hydrogen cyanide leads to mandelic acid, the benzoin condensation gives benzoin, a cross aldol with ethanal gives cinnamaldehyde, the flavour of cinnamon, and condensation with dimethylaniline leads to the dye malachite green.

slides.heading: Quick check: distinguishing tests
slides.body_md: Choose a test that distinguishes benzaldehyde from an aliphatic aldehyde.
slides.narration: Quick check. Fehling’s solution and the iodoform test both work for ethanal but not for benzaldehyde.

slides.heading: Summary: Part 2
bullets: Benzaldehyde vs ethanal: Fehling’s and iodoform negative for benzaldehyde; both reduce Tollens’.

visual.alt: Summary table of named reactions

slides.narration: Let us sum up Part 2. Having no alpha hydrogen, benzaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated alkali, the benzoin condensation with cyanide, and the Perkin reaction with acetic anhydride. Its aldehyde group deactivates the ring and directs substitution to the meta position. It is distinguished from aliphatic aldehydes by the Fehling’s and iodoform tests.

slides.heading: Exam tips: Part 2
bullets: Give the catalyst/conditions for each named reaction (conc. alkali; KCN in ethanol; CH₃COONa at 453 K).
Explain meta direction with the σ-complex argument.
For tests, describe results with both compounds.

visual.alt: Table of three common slips in Part 2 and fixes

slides.narration: Final tips. Always give the reagents and conditions that identify each named reaction. Remember that the Perkin reaction gives cinnamic acid. Explain meta direction using the intermediate. And when distinguishing compounds, describe what happens with each one.

notes.title: Benzaldehyde — Notes

sections.heading: 1. Preparation and physical properties
sections.body_md:
C₆H₅CHO: –CHO conjugated with the ring; **no α-H**.

**Etard reaction:** toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ (CS₂/CCl₄) → brown complex → H₂O → benzaldehyde (oxidation stops at CHO). Also: toluene + 2Cl₂ (hν) → C₆H₅CHCl₂ → (H₂O, 373 K) C₆H₅CHO; Gattermann–Koch: C₆H₆ + CO (HCl, AlCl₃/CuCl).

**Properties:** colourless oily liquid, bitter-almond smell, b.p. 452 K, density 1.04 g cm⁻³, slightly soluble in water; air-oxidised to benzoic acid.

key_terms.definition_md: Oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde by chromyl chloride.

visual.alt: Table of preparations

sections.heading: 2. Oxidation, reduction and addition reactions
sections.body_md:
**Oxidation:** air, K₂Cr₂O₇/H⁺, KMnO₄ → benzoic acid; Tollens’ → silver mirror; **Fehling’s: no reaction**.
**Reduction:** H₂/Ni, NaBH₄, LiAlH₄ → benzyl alcohol; Clemmensen or Wolff–Kishner → toluene.
**Addition:** HCN → mandelonitrile C₆H₅CH(OH)CN → (H₃O⁺) mandelic acid; NaHSO₃ → crystalline adduct.
**Ammonia derivatives:** NH₂OH → benzaldoxime; NH₂NH₂ → hydrazone; C₆H₅NHNH₂ → phenylhydrazone. **PCl₅** → benzal chloride C₆H₅CHCl₂.

sections.heading: 3. Cannizzaro, benzoin and Perkin reactions
sections.body_md:
**Cannizzaro** (conc. NaOH): $\ce{2C6H5CHO + NaOH -> C6H5CH2OH + C6H5COONa}$ (hydride transfer). Crossed with HCHO: benzaldehyde → benzyl alcohol, HCHO → HCOONa.
**Benzoin condensation** (KCN in ethanol, catalytic CN⁻): $\ce{2C6H5CHO -> C6H5CH(OH)COC6H5}$.
**Perkin** ((CH₃CO)₂O + CH₃COONa, 453 K): $\ce{C6H5CHO + (CH3CO)2O -> C6H5CH=CHCOOH + CH3COOH}$ (cinnamic acid).

key_terms.definition_md: 3-Phenylprop-2-enoic acid, product of the Perkin reaction.

visual.alt: Table of named reactions

sections.heading: 4. Ring substitution, tests and uses
sections.body_md:
–CHO: −I, −R → **deactivating, meta directing**. Nitration (cold) → 3-nitrobenzaldehyde; Cl₂/FeCl₃ → 3-chlorobenzaldehyde; fuming H₂SO₄ → 3-formylbenzenesulphonic acid.

**Benzaldehyde vs ethanal:** Fehling’s (ethanal +, benzaldehyde −); iodoform (ethanal +); dilute alkali (ethanal aldol); conc. alkali (benzaldehyde Cannizzaro); both give Tollens’.

**Uses:** flavouring (almond), perfumes, dyes (malachite green), cinnamic acid, cinnamaldehyde (cross aldol with ethanal), mandelic acid, benzoin.

key_terms.definition_md: An electron-withdrawing substituent that directs incoming electrophiles to the meta position.

visual.alt: Table of distinguishing tests

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Using KMnO₄ to convert toluene to benzaldehyde (gives benzoic acid).
- Saying benzaldehyde reduces Fehling’s solution.
- Giving o/p products for ring substitution (–CHO is meta directing).
- Confusing benzal chloride (C₆H₅CHCl₂) with benzoyl chloride (C₆H₅COCl).

**How marks are usually awarded**
- Named reactions (1–2 marks): reagents, conditions, balanced equation and product name.
- Meta direction (2 marks): electron withdrawal and σ-complex argument.
- Distinguishing tests (1–2 marks): reagent and results for both compounds.

cards.front_md: Exam tip: benzal vs benzoyl chloride
cards.back_md: PCl₅ on C₆H₅CHO → C₆H₅CHCl₂; on C₆H₅COOH → C₆H₅COCl.

questions.stem_md: In the Etard reaction, toluene is converted into benzaldehyde by:

options.text_md: hot alkaline KMnO₄, followed by acidification
chlorine in the dark with FeCl₃
chromyl chloride in CS₂, followed by hydrolysis of the brown complex

questions.solution_md: CrO₂Cl₂ oxidises the CH₃ group only as far as CHO — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Boiling toluene is treated with chlorine in sunlight until two chlorine atoms have entered, and the product is heated with water at 373 K. The final product is:
questions.solution_md: C₆H₅CHCl₂ (benzal chloride) is hydrolysed to C₆H₅CHO — option (b).

questions.stem_md: In the Gattermann–Koch reaction, benzene is converted into benzaldehyde using:

options.text_md: CO and HCl with anhydrous AlCl₃ and CuCl

questions.stem_md: White crystals form around the stopper of an old bottle of benzaldehyde. They are most probably:

options.text_md: benzoic acid, formed by air oxidation

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is a colourless oily liquid with the smell of bitter ___.
True or false? Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen atom.
questions.solution_md: True. The carbon next to C=O is a ring carbon bearing no hydrogen.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Hot alkaline KMnO₄ is not used to convert toluene into benzaldehyde.

**Reason (R):** KMnO₄ oxidises the side chain of toluene all the way to the –COOH group.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and R explains A — option (a).

questions.stem_md: $9.2\ \text{g}$ of toluene ($M = 92$) is converted into benzaldehyde ($M = 106$) by the Etard reaction with a 60% yield. What mass of benzaldehyde is obtained?
Write equations for preparing benzaldehyde from toluene via benzal chloride, giving the conditions.

answer.model_answer_md: $\ce{C6H5CH3 + 2Cl2 ->[h\nu][boiling toluene] C6H5CHCl2 + 2HCl}$; $\ce{C6H5CHCl2 + H2O ->[373 K] C6H5CHO + 2HCl}$.

questions.stem_md: State two physical properties of benzaldehyde and explain why it should be stored in a tightly closed bottle.

answer.model_answer_md: Colourless oily liquid with a smell of bitter almonds; b.p. 452 K; slightly soluble in water, miscible with organic solvents (any two). It is slowly oxidised by air to benzoic acid, so air must be excluded.

questions.stem_md: Describe the Etard reaction for preparing benzaldehyde from toluene, explaining why the oxidation stops at the aldehyde, and give one other method of making benzaldehyde from benzene.

answer.model_answer_md: Toluene is treated with chromyl chloride (CrO₂Cl₂) in CS₂ or CCl₄; a brown chromium complex (Etard complex) precipitates. Hydrolysis with water gives benzaldehyde. The aldehyde is bound in the complex, so it is not oxidised further until it is released by hydrolysis. From benzene: Gattermann–Koch reaction — CO and HCl with anhydrous AlCl₃/CuCl.

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is warmed separately with Tollens’ reagent and with Fehling’s solution. The results are:

options.text_md: a silver mirror and a red-brown precipitate
a silver mirror with Tollens’ reagent; no change with Fehling’s solution

questions.solution_md: Aromatic aldehydes reduce Tollens’ but not Fehling’s — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde reacts with HCN in the presence of a little base. The product, hydrolysed with dilute acid, gives:
questions.solution_md: Mandelonitrile, C₆H₅CH(OH)CN, hydrolyses to mandelic acid — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is treated with phosphorus pentachloride. The organic product is:
questions.solution_md: PCl₅ replaces the carbonyl O by two Cl — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde reacts with hydroxylamine. The product is:
questions.solution_md: Addition then loss of water — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is reduced with sodium borohydride. The product is:
Benzaldehyde is heated with zinc amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid. The product is:
Benzaldehyde is slightly less reactive than ethanal towards nucleophilic addition. The main reason is that:

options.text_md: the ring makes the carbonyl carbon sp³
conjugation with the ring reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon

questions.solution_md: Electron donation from the ring by resonance lowers δ+ on C — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling’s solution.

**Reason (R):** Benzaldehyde is not oxidised by any reagent.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: A is true. R is false: benzaldehyde is oxidised by air, Tollens’ reagent and KMnO₄ — option (c).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Benzaldehyde can be separated from a mixture with toluene by shaking with saturated sodium hydrogensulphite solution.
questions.solution_md: True. Benzaldehyde forms a crystalline bisulphite adduct; toluene does not.

questions.stem_md: The cyanohydrin formed when HCN adds to benzaldehyde is called ___.
Match each reagent used on benzaldehyde with the product.
questions.solution_md: Phenylhydrazine → phenylhydrazone; PCl₅ → C₆H₅CHCl₂; H₂/Ni → C₆H₅CH₂OH; NaHSO₃ → adduct.

questions.stem_md: $1.06\ \text{g}$ of benzaldehyde ($M = 106$) is warmed with excess Tollens’ reagent: $\ce{C6H5CHO + 2[Ag(NH3)2]+ + 3OH- -> C6H5COO- + 2Ag + 2H2O + 4NH3}$. What mass of silver ($M = 108$) is deposited?
Write the equation for the air oxidation of benzaldehyde and name one reagent that oxidises benzaldehyde in the laboratory.

answer.model_answer_md: $\ce{2C6H5CHO + O2 -> 2C6H5COOH}$ (benzoic acid). Laboratory oxidants: acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, alkaline KMnO₄ (then acid), or Tollens’ reagent.

questions.stem_md: Write equations for the reaction of benzaldehyde with (a) hydrazine and (b) phenylhydrazine, naming the products.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) $\ce{C6H5CHO + NH2NH2 -> C6H5CH=NNH2 + H2O}$: benzaldehyde hydrazone. (b) $\ce{C6H5CHO + C6H5NHNH2 -> C6H5CH=NNHC6H5 + H2O}$: benzaldehyde phenylhydrazone.

questions.stem_md: Give the product when benzaldehyde is treated with (a) LiAlH₄, (b) hydrazine followed by KOH in ethylene glycol on heating and (c) HCN followed by acid hydrolysis.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Benzyl alcohol, C₆H₅CH₂OH. (b) Toluene, C₆H₅CH₃ (Wolff–Kishner). (c) Mandelic acid, C₆H₅CH(OH)COOH.

questions.stem_md: Write equations for benzaldehyde with (a) sodium hydrogensulphite, (b) hydroxylamine and (c) phosphorus pentachloride.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) $\ce{C6H5CHO + NaHSO3 -> C6H5CH(OH)SO3Na}$. (b) $\ce{C6H5CHO + NH2OH -> C6H5CH=NOH + H2O}$. (c) $\ce{C6H5CHO + PCl5 -> C6H5CHCl2 + POCl3}$.

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is heated with acetic anhydride and anhydrous sodium acetate at about 453 K. The organic acid formed is:
Benzaldehyde is warmed with potassium cyanide in aqueous ethanol. The product is:
questions.solution_md: Benzoin condensation; CN⁻ is only a catalyst — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is shaken with 50% aqueous KOH. The products are:
The key step in the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde is the transfer of:

options.text_md: a hydride ion from one aldehyde-derived anion to a second benzaldehyde molecule

questions.solution_md: H⁻ transfer reduces one molecule and oxidises the other — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A mixture of benzaldehyde and methanal is treated with concentrated NaOH. Benzaldehyde is converted mainly into:
questions.solution_md: Crossed Cannizzaro: methanal is oxidised, benzaldehyde reduced — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Benzaldehyde gives the Cannizzaro reaction but not aldol condensation.

**Reason (R):** Benzaldehyde has no α-hydrogen, so it cannot form an enolate ion.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true; R explains A — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** In the benzoin condensation, cyanide ion acts as a catalyst.

**Reason (R):** Cyanide ion is a strong oxidising agent.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: A is true (CN⁻ is regenerated). R is false — option (c).

questions.stem_md: True or false? In the Perkin reaction, sodium acetate acts as a base that removes an α-hydrogen from acetic anhydride.
questions.solution_md: True. The resulting anion attacks the benzaldehyde carbonyl.

questions.stem_md: $21.2\ \text{g}$ of benzaldehyde ($M = 106$) undergoes complete Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH. What mass of benzyl alcohol ($M = 108$) forms?
$10.6\ \text{g}$ of benzaldehyde ($M = 106$) is converted by the Perkin reaction into cinnamic acid ($M = 148$) with a 70% yield. What mass of cinnamic acid is obtained?
Write the equation for the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde, and explain how the two products are separated and the acid obtained.

answer.model_answer_md: $\ce{2C6H5CHO + NaOH -> C6H5CH2OH + C6H5COONa}$. Benzyl alcohol is extracted with ether (sodium benzoate stays in water); acidifying the aqueous layer with HCl precipitates benzoic acid.

questions.stem_md: Write the equation for the benzoin condensation and name the functional groups present in benzoin.

answer.model_answer_md: $\ce{2C6H5CHO ->[KCN][ethanol] C6H5CH(OH)COC6H5}$. Benzoin contains a secondary alcohol (–CH(OH)–) and a ketone (–CO–) group: it is an α-hydroxy ketone.

questions.stem_md: Write the equation for the Perkin reaction of benzaldehyde, naming the reagents’ roles and the product.

answer.model_answer_md: $\ce{C6H5CHO + (CH3CO)2O ->[CH3COONa][453 K] C6H5CH=CHCOOH + CH3COOH}$. Acetic anhydride supplies the α-carbon; sodium acetate is the base catalyst; product: cinnamic acid (3-phenylprop-2-enoic acid).

questions.stem_md: Identify the reaction and give the product for benzaldehyde with (a) conc. NaOH, (b) KCN in ethanol and (c) acetic anhydride with sodium acetate at 453 K.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Cannizzaro: benzyl alcohol + sodium benzoate. (b) Benzoin condensation: benzoin. (c) Perkin reaction: cinnamic acid.

questions.stem_md: Outline the mechanism of the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde and explain why ethanal does not give this reaction.

answer.model_answer_md: OH⁻ adds to the carbonyl carbon of one benzaldehyde molecule, giving a tetrahedral anion. This anion transfers a hydride ion (H⁻) to the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule, becoming benzoic acid while the second becomes the benzyloxide ion. Proton exchange gives benzoate and benzyl alcohol. Ethanal has α-hydrogens; with alkali it forms an enolate and undergoes aldol reactions instead.

questions.solution_md: OH⁻ addition; hydride transfer; ethanal aldol.

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde is nitrated with a mixture of concentrated nitric and sulphuric acids in the cold. The major product is:
The –CHO group directs electrophiles to the meta position because:

options.text_md: it donates electrons by resonance to o and p positions
it is too large to allow o/p attack
it withdraws electrons, and o/p attack would place positive charge next to it in the σ-complex

questions.solution_md: Meta attack avoids the destabilised resonance form — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Which test gives a positive result with ethanal but not with benzaldehyde?
questions.solution_md: Benzaldehyde does not reduce Fehling’s solution — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde and ethanal are each warmed with iodine and NaOH. The observation is:

options.text_md: ethanal gives a yellow precipitate; benzaldehyde does not
benzaldehyde gives a yellow precipitate; ethanal does not

questions.stem_md: Benzaldehyde reacts with chlorine in the presence of anhydrous FeCl₃. The major product is:
questions.solution_md: Ring substitution, meta to CHO — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Cinnamaldehyde, the flavour of cinnamon, is made from benzaldehyde by:

options.text_md: cross aldol condensation with ethanal in dilute alkali

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Nitration of benzaldehyde is slower than nitration of benzene.

**Reason (R):** The –CHO group donates electrons to the ring by resonance.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: A is true (–CHO deactivates). R is false: –CHO withdraws electrons — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Nitration of benzaldehyde is carried out at low temperature.

**Reason (R):** Hot concentrated nitric acid would oxidise the –CHO group to –COOH.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md: Both are true and R explains A — option (a).

questions.stem_md: True or false? Both benzaldehyde and ethanal give a silver mirror with Tollens’ reagent.
questions.solution_md: True. Tollens’ reagent cannot distinguish them; Fehling’s or iodoform can.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Bromination of benzaldehyde with Br₂/FeBr₃ gives mainly 4-bromobenzaldehyde.
Benzaldehyde condenses with N,N-dimethylaniline in the manufacture of the dye malachite ___.
Explain why the –CHO group is meta directing and deactivating in electrophilic substitution of benzaldehyde.

answer.model_answer_md: The –CHO group withdraws electrons from the ring by −I and −R effects, lowering electron density (deactivation). In the σ-complexes for ortho and para attack, one resonance form places the positive charge on the carbon bearing the electron-withdrawing –CHO group, which is very unfavourable; meta attack avoids this, so meta substitution is preferred.

questions.stem_md: Give two chemical tests, with observations, that distinguish benzaldehyde from ethanal.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) Fehling’s solution, warm: ethanal gives a red-brown precipitate of Cu₂O; benzaldehyde does not react. (ii) I₂ + NaOH, warm: ethanal gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform; benzaldehyde does not.

questions.stem_md: Write equations for (a) the nitration and (b) the chlorination of benzaldehyde, naming the major products, and (c) explain why the nitration is done in the cold.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) $\ce{C6H5CHO + HNO3 ->[conc. H2SO4][273-283 K] O2NC6H4CHO + H2O}$: 3-nitrobenzaldehyde. (b) $\ce{C6H5CHO + Cl2 ->[FeCl3] ClC6H4CHO + HCl}$: 3-chlorobenzaldehyde. (c) At higher temperature nitric acid would oxidise –CHO to –COOH.

questions.stem_md: Name the compound made from benzaldehyde in each case and give one use: (a) by the Perkin reaction, (b) by cross aldol condensation with ethanal and (c) by addition of HCN followed by hydrolysis.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Cinnamic acid — perfumes and flavourings (esters). (b) Cinnamaldehyde — cinnamon flavour. (c) Mandelic acid — in skin-care products and as a urinary antiseptic (any reasonable use).

questions.stem_md:
(a) Describe the Etard reaction for converting toluene into benzaldehyde. [1½]

(b) Write equations for the reaction of benzaldehyde with (i) HCN, (ii) NaHSO₃ and (iii) PCl₅. [2]

(c) Explain why benzaldehyde reduces Tollens’ reagent but not Fehling’s solution, and give the product of its reduction with NaBH₄. [1½]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Toluene + CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂ gives a brown chromium complex; hydrolysis with water gives benzaldehyde; oxidation stops at the aldehyde.

(b) (i) $\ce{C6H5CHO + HCN -> C6H5CH(OH)CN}$. (ii) $\ce{C6H5CHO + NaHSO3 -> C6H5CH(OH)SO3Na}$. (iii) $\ce{C6H5CHO + PCl5 -> C6H5CHCl2 + POCl3}$.

(c) The –CHO group of benzaldehyde is conjugated with the ring, which makes it harder to oxidise than an aliphatic –CHO. Ammoniacal Ag⁺ (Tollens’) is able to oxidise it, but the weaker Cu²⁺ tartrate complex in Fehling’s solution is not, so no Cu₂O forms. NaBH₄ gives benzyl alcohol.

questions.solution_md: Etard; three equations; Tollens’ vs Fehling’s.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Write equations for the Cannizzaro, benzoin and Perkin reactions of benzaldehyde, giving the reagents and conditions. [3]

(b) Why does benzaldehyde undergo the Cannizzaro reaction rather than aldol condensation? [1]

(c) What happens when benzaldehyde and methanal are treated together with concentrated NaOH? [1]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Cannizzaro: $\ce{2C6H5CHO + NaOH -> C6H5CH2OH + C6H5COONa}$ (conc. alkali). Benzoin: $\ce{2C6H5CHO ->[KCN][ethanol] C6H5CH(OH)COC6H5}$. Perkin: $\ce{C6H5CHO + (CH3CO)2O ->[CH3COONa][453 K] C6H5CH=CHCOOH + CH3COOH}$.

(b) It has no α-hydrogen, so no enolate can form.

(c) Crossed Cannizzaro: $\ce{C6H5CHO + HCHO + NaOH -> C6H5CH2OH + HCOONa}$ — benzaldehyde is reduced, methanal oxidised.

questions.solution_md: Three named reactions; no α-H; crossed Cannizzaro.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Explain, with reference to the intermediate, why the –CHO group is meta directing. [2]

(b) Write equations for the nitration and chlorination of benzaldehyde. [2]

(c) Give two uses of benzaldehyde. [1]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) –CHO withdraws electrons (−I, −R). In the σ-complex for ortho or para attack, one resonance structure places + on the ring carbon bonded to the electron-withdrawing –CHO group, which is strongly destabilised; for meta attack no such structure exists. So the meta σ-complex is the least unstable, and meta substitution predominates (though slower than in benzene).

(b) $\ce{C6H5CHO + HNO3 ->[H2SO4][cold] O2NC6H4CHO + H2O}$ (3-nitrobenzaldehyde); $\ce{C6H5CHO + Cl2 ->[FeCl3] ClC6H4CHO + HCl}$ (3-chlorobenzaldehyde).

(c) Flavouring (almond); perfumery; manufacture of dyes (malachite green), cinnamic acid, mandelic acid.

questions.stem_md:
An aromatic compound A, C₇H₆O, gives a silver mirror with Tollens’ reagent but no precipitate with Fehling’s solution. With concentrated NaOH, A gives B and C; C on acidification gives D, C₇H₆O₂. A with KCN in ethanol gives E, C₁₄H₁₂O₂.

(a) Identify A to E. [4]

(b) Write the equation for the formation of E. [1]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A: benzaldehyde, C₆H₅CHO. B: benzyl alcohol, C₆H₅CH₂OH. C: sodium benzoate, C₆H₅COONa. D: benzoic acid, C₆H₅COOH. E: benzoin, C₆H₅CH(OH)COC₆H₅.

(b) $\ce{2C6H5CHO ->[KCN][ethanol] C6H5CH(OH)COC6H5}$.

questions.solution_md: Benzaldehyde, benzyl alcohol, sodium benzoate, benzoic acid, benzoin.

questions.stem_md:
How would you carry out the following conversions? Give reagents and conditions. [1 each]

(a) Toluene to benzaldehyde

(b) Benzaldehyde to cinnamic acid

(c) Benzaldehyde to benzoin

(d) Benzaldehyde to 3-nitrobenzaldehyde

(e) Benzaldehyde to toluene

answer.model_answer_md: (a) CrO₂Cl₂ in CS₂, then H₂O (Etard). (b) (CH₃CO)₂O + CH₃COONa, 453 K (Perkin). (c) KCN in aqueous ethanol, warm (benzoin condensation). (d) Conc. HNO₃ + conc. H₂SO₄, cold. (e) Zn–Hg + conc. HCl (Clemmensen) or NH₂NH₂ then KOH/ethylene glycol.

questions.stem_md: Compare benzaldehyde and ethanal in their behaviour with (a) Fehling’s solution, (b) dilute NaOH and (c) concentrated NaOH, giving reasons.

answer.model_answer_md: (a) Ethanal reduces Fehling’s solution (red-brown Cu₂O); benzaldehyde does not, because its conjugated –CHO is harder to oxidise. (b) Ethanal, which has α-hydrogens, undergoes aldol condensation; benzaldehyde has no α-H and does not. (c) Benzaldehyde undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (benzyl alcohol + sodium benzoate); ethanal gives aldol products and resins instead.
